standard.title: Reflect to refine production choices
standard.description: reflect on their own or others' media arts works and/or practices to refine and inform choices they make during stages of the production process
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can document and explain production choices and use Viewpoints questions to evaluate communicative intent. They have used editing software to experiment with sequences. They have not yet applied systematic reflective practice that informs refinement across all stages of production — or developed DSLR manual camera skills through reflective practice.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on their own or others' media arts works and practices to refine and inform choices across stages of the production process.

nodes.label: Analytical reflection on practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse existing media arts works — examining how camera work, sound, editing, media technologies and mise-en-scène construct representations — and use this analysis to inform their own practice.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse how at least three technical elements in an existing media arts work construct conventional or alternative representations — and document how at least one finding will inform a decision in their own production.
nodes.typical_width: Use Viewpoints questions to examine how camera work, sound, editing and mise-en-scène construct representations in a genre, auteur's work or film movement; document findings; identify which techniques to apply, subvert or challenge in original production; connect analysis to production decisions explicitly.
wider: Examine how camera work, sound, editing and mise-en-scène in a specific film movement or auteur's work construct conventional representations — then design and produce a media arts work that communicates alternative representations to audiences, documenting how each analytical finding informed each production decision

Analyse a media arts work that has been critically recognised for challenging dominant representations — identifying the specific technical and symbolic strategies used, and applying at least two strategies in original production work
nodes.hinge_reason: Analytical reflection is the mechanism that converts existing media arts knowledge into production improvement — without it, students produce technically competent works that are not critically informed, and the 'reflect to refine' command term is not met.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions as the analytical framework: 'How has camera work been manipulated to construct this representation? What would change if I used a different approach?' The reasoning chain analysis→finding→application is the core skill.

success_criteria: Student analyses at least three technical elements in a media arts work and explains how they construct representations
Student documents at least one analytical finding and explains how it will inform a production decision

nodes.label: Reflective practice across production stages
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply reflective practice across multiple stages of their own production — documenting decisions, evaluating against intent, and refining based on analysis.
nodes.minimum_width: Document production decisions at two or more stages of a production process — evaluating at each stage whether decisions are serving the intended communicative goal, and describing at least one refinement made as a result.
nodes.typical_width: Apply systematic reflective practice across pre-production, production and post-production; document and explain creative choices in relation to representations and genre codes; use editing software to experiment with sequences, applying technical codes deliberately; develop manual camera skills (ISO, shutter speed, aperture) through reflective experimentation.
wider: Use editing software to experiment systematically with multiple versions of the same sequence — applying different technical codes (filters, text, music, rhythm, pace) and comparing how each creates meaning for audiences before selecting and justifying the final approach

Develop DSLR manual camera skills through structured reflective practice — documenting ISO, shutter speed and aperture experiments across different lighting conditions, reflecting on how manual control serves intended meaning, and applying findings to original production work

response_modes.reason: Build reflective practice across production stages — students who only reflect at the end produce works that could have been much stronger with earlier intervention. Practise mid-production reflection as a production skill.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of reflective practice opportunities at Y9-10 (editing software experimentation, DSLR manual skills, multi-version comparison, genre homage, auteur analysis) is genuinely rich — students who practise across multiple reflection types develop much more sophisticated production self-awareness.
success_criteria: Student documents production decisions at two or more stages of a production
Student describes at least one refinement made as a result of mid-production reflection, with an explanation of the reasoning
